title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join a major speech-recognition leaderboard
summary: Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard, a public ranking of how accurately AI tools turn speech into text, now tests models on Egyptian and Nigerian English.

title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
summary: Google has introduced Gemini Omni 1.

title: A cheaper AI 'judge' that asks Opus for help matches Opus at a quarter of the cost
summary: Data company Hightouch describes using a smaller AI model to check whether two customer records belong to the same person, calling on Anthropic's larger Opus model only when it's unsure.

title: RealPage rent-pricing case ends with nearly $360M for renters
summary: A legal case over RealPage's rent-pricing software — accused of helping landlords push rents up by feeding them shared pricing recommendations — has wrapped up with nearly $360 million going to renters.

title: US air traffic control will stop using floppy disks by 2028
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration says it will phase out floppy disks from its air traffic control systems by 2028, Reuters reports.

title: NVIDIA adds four open Cosmos 3 models for simulated worlds
summary: NVIDIA's Cosmos platform for 'world models' — AI that generates realistic, interactive simulations of physical environments — has added four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 family.

title: ToyBlocks: a controlled test world for robot learning
summary: The Allen Institute for AI introduced ToyBlocks, a controlled environment for training and evaluating robots.

title: Brain-wave headsets may be collecting your brain data to train AI
summary: A report in Science says makers of consumer brain-wave headsets — wearables sold for meditation, focus or sleep — are harvesting users' brain data to train AI, without telling them.

title: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" option has leaked passwords into 1,122 public files
summary: Security firm Apiiro reports that Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" permission option has led to passwords and other secrets ending up in 1,122 public files on GitHub.

title: Your Mac may be quietly sorting people into family members
summary: A widely shared write-up says every Mac ships with an undocumented classifier — a small AI that sorts things into categories — that guesses which people in your life are family, as part of Apple Intelligence's personal knowledge graph.

title: Apple's 'grey list' of words your iPhone won't help you spell
summary: The Guardian reports that iPhones keep a grey list of words and phrases that autocorrect and suggestions won't help you type — including some perfectly ordinary insults.

title: A law firm explains how it runs entirely on free software
summary: UK firm decoded.

title: Mistral Large 4 lands on Hugging Face
summary: French AI company Mistral's Large 4 model — nicknamed 'Le Chonk' — is now available on Hugging Face, the main public hub for sharing AI models.

title: MaxxBench asks whether AI coding scores can be trusted
summary: A new benchmark project, MaxxBench, opens with a pointed question about a popular AI coding test: "Nice DeepSWE score.

title: Outlook.com is quietly rejecting email from domains without DMARC
summary: A widely shared report from email provider MailRoute says Outlook.

title: Goldman Sachs is pulling Claude Code from its bankers and traders
summary: A report says Goldman Sachs is taking Anthropic's AI coding assistant, Claude Code, away from staff in its banking and trading teams.

title: Anthropic maps out possible futures for an AI economy
summary: Anthropic published 'Scenarios for our economic future', which starts from a plain admission: nobody knows yet whether AI will bring rapid growth, widespread unemployment, neither, or something else.

title: A security researcher says one car brand's vehicles can be unlocked worldwide
summary: A widely discussed write-up titled 'Unlocking any car from X brand in most of the world' describes a security flaw that a researcher says affects one car maker's vehicles in most countries.

title: How one writer fights 'AI brain fry'
summary: A popular blog post describes the mental fatigue of working with AI tools all day and the habits the author uses to stay sharp.

title: Llama-modchip runs a 284-billion-parameter DeepSeek model on 64GB of RAM, no GPU
summary: An open-source project called llama-modchip says it can run a 284-billion-parameter DeepSeek model on a machine with 64GB of ordinary memory and no graphics card.

title: GitHub has copied almost every repository to Azure on the way to 'agent-scale' Git
summary: Previously covered on 2026-11-06: GitHub described a new Git storage design built so thousands of AI agents can push to one repository at once.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic has upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos, the models it builds for its hardest technical work, saying the 5.

title: Claim: Gemini sends some personal Drive files and emails to human reviewers
summary: A GitHub repository that drew wide attention on Hacker News claims that Google Gemini routes personal Google Drive files and emails to human annotators, the people who review AI output to improve it.

title: Canada launches Real-Time Rail, a 24/7 instant payment system
summary: Payments Canada has launched Real-Time Rail, a national system that lets money move between accounts instantly, any hour of any day.

title: Meta introduces Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model
summary: Meta has released Muse Ember, which it calls the smallest and most efficient model in its Muse family.

title: Parking apps charge a median $0.35 convenience fee per session
summary: A new dataset from ParkGraph tracks the extra convenience fees parking apps add in 312 US cities, and finds a typical charge of 35 cents each time you park.

title: HOPE: shrinking 'mixture-of-experts' models by keeping expert partners together
summary: Amazon researchers describe HOPE, a method for pruning mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.

title: E-means claims to beat k-means in a tenth of the training passes
summary: A new clustering method called E-means says it outperforms k-means, the classic algorithm for grouping similar data points, while needing only one-tenth as many epochs, or full passes over the data.

title: AI bug-hunting project Glasswing is swamping volunteer maintainers, report says
summary: Security firm VulnCheck reviewed seven months of Project Glasswing, Anthropic's effort to use AI to find security flaws in widely used open-source software, and says it has overwhelmed the volunteers who maintain that software with findings that are mostly underwhelming.

title: From a health worker's notebook to the Ebola response
summary: Anthropic published 'The Situation Report', a feature on the Ebola response in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: People use AI to find news, but don't want it writing the news
summary: Nieman Lab reports that AI is becoming a common gateway to information, yet audiences still don't want AI producing the journalism itself.

title: Hugging Face can now go on your Google Cloud bill
summary: Organizations can link their Hugging Face account to Google Cloud so usage appears on their existing Google Cloud bill instead of a credit card.

title: A large study measures how easily websites can recognise you
summary: A new study looks at how 'fingerprintable' web users are — how easily sites can identify you from details of your browser and device, without cookies.

title: Git patches six security vulnerabilities
summary: Git, the version-control tool almost all software teams use to track changes, released updates fixing six security vulnerabilities.

title: Hugging Face adds 'decision models' for problems that aren't about text
summary: Hugging Face introduced Decision Models, starting from the point that large language models excel at generating text but many problems don't need text at all — they need a choice, a score or an action.

title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights for travelers
summary: United Airlines has barred AI agents — assistants that browse and buy on your behalf — from booking flights for its customers, CBS News reports.

title: A personal AI assistant small enough to run on your own device
summary: BotPsy is an AI assistant built on a model with under a billion parameters, small enough to run directly on your phone or laptop instead of in the cloud.

title: Yogurt: a free, private, open-source AI meeting notetaker
summary: A new open-source project called Yogurt pitches itself as a free and private alternative to Granola, the popular AI meeting-notes app.

title: Critical security flaw found in Apache, a widely used web server
summary: Security firm Wiz reports a critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server — software that powers a large share of the world's websites — that could let attackers run their own code on affected servers.

title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API
summary: Google has announced a Gemini Decisions API for developers, a tool aimed at having AI make choices rather than write text.

title: Shrinking AI search indexes with token pooling
summary: Multi-vector embedding models power a precise kind of AI search: each word in your query gets its own chance to match something in a document.

title: GitHub's guide to 'agentic engineering'
summary: GitHub published a guide arguing that while writing code got faster with AI, the work around it — planning, reviewing changes, investigating production issues — didn't.

title: Google introduces Gemini 4 Hydrogen
summary: Google has announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new model in its Gemini AI family.

title: Edge0-145B promises frontier AI on your own computer
summary: A company called Edge0 has introduced Edge0-145B, a 145-billion-parameter model it says brings frontier AI capabilities to a personal computer.

title: AI is making Apple's app review a nightmare for music-software makers
summary: Synth Anatomy reports that developers of synthesizer and music apps are struggling with Apple's app review process, which they say AI is now making harder.

title: Jane Street is changing its software engineering interviews
summary: Trading firm Jane Street says its software engineering interviews are "changing a little".

title: Brave lets AI agents pay for search on their own
summary: Brave's Search API now accepts payments from AI agents through a protocol called x402, so an assistant can pay for the searches it runs without a person entering card details.

title: LLMON: a markup language built for AI models, now in IBM's Granite 4.1
summary: IBM introduced LLMON, a markup language designed for how large language models read their context.

title: GitHub's guide to agent skills that work in any AI tool
summary: GitHub published a practical guide to agent skills: files that capture repeatable engineering work so teams can review and reuse them.

title: llama.cpp, the engine behind much of 'local AI', hits version 1.0
summary: llama.

title: US flights halted nationwide for 4.5 hours
summary: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on departing flights, lifting it about 4.

title: XYBench tests whether AI can help when you ask the wrong question
summary: The Allen Institute for AI released XYBench, a set of more than 8,000 questions built on misconceptions, to test whether assistants spot the real problem behind a request.

title: Security agencies found using an ad-based surveillance system
summary: Researchers at Citizen Lab report that security agencies in several countries use a surveillance system built on online advertising data.

title: Accessibility statements get a home on GitHub
summary: GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.

title: GitHub's October outages: eight incidents, up from two
summary: GitHub's monthly availability report says it had eight incidents in October 2026 that degraded performance across its services, compared with two in September.
